audits.title: An audit to assess and improve the quality of referrals received by Community Dental Services from General Dental Practitioners for the one-off treatments of patients under 18 years, with inhalation sedation and general anaesthesia, in Salford
audits.standard: Referral quality/acceptance for inhalation sedation and general anaesthesia; no numeric target stated
audits.setting: Community Dental Services, Salford (paediatric sedation and general anaesthesia referrals)

cycle1.result: 48% acceptance rate; most referrals had 2 errors; almost 2 in 5 inhalation sedation referrals not justified appropriately or lacked a diagnosis.

audits.intervention: Contacted the triaging hub and local GDPs and created local triaging guidance.
audits.other_findings: Authors state further quality improvement projects are needed for sustainable change.
audits.citation: Bharadia T, Gnanasekharan L. An audit to assess and improve the quality of referrals received by Community Dental Services from General Dental Practitioners for the one-off treatments of patients under 18 years, with inhalation sedation and general anaesthesia, in Salford. . 2023. doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-3083133/v1.

audits.title: An audit of the quality and content of periodontal referrals and the effect of implementing referral criteria.
audits.setting: Periodontal department of a teaching hospital, Eastman Dental Hospital, London

cycle1.result: Use of Basic Periodontal Examination (BPE) score in referrals 17%; medical history mentioned in 31-34% of letters.

audits.intervention: Referral guidelines implemented (2000/2001), then referral criteria redefined and circulated via Primary Care Trusts (2004/2005).

cycle2.result: BPE score use 57%; medical history still mentioned in only 31-34% of letters; clinical details had increased in 2000/2001 with a tendency to decrease in 2004/2005.

audits.other_findings: 450 referrals across three periods (1997, 2000/2001, 2004/2005). Little agreement between referral clinical details and consultation findings; a pro forma was not associated with better referral quality.
audits.citation: Kourkouta S, Darbar UR. An audit of the quality and content of periodontal referrals and the effect of implementing referral criteria. Prim Dent Care. 2006;13(3):99-106. doi:10.1308/135576106777795590. PMID: 16836813.

audits.title: An audit of orthodontic referrals using IOTN as a comparison.
audits.setting: Regional orthodontic units, HSE North Eastern division

cycle1.result: 97% of patients in IOTN DHC grades 4 or 5.

audits.intervention: Recommendations from 2003 audit on referral form completion and study model quality.

cycle2.result: 100% in DHC grades 4 or 5; mean 63.5% in AC grades 8 to 10.

audits.other_findings: Recommendations on referral forms and study model quality were found effective.
audits.citation: O'Hanrahan S, Macauley D. An audit of orthodontic referrals using IOTN as a comparison. J Ir Dent Assoc. 2007;53(1):29-31. PMID: 17396763.

audits.title: An audit of letters of referral to a prosthodontic department in a dental teaching hospital.
audits.standard: Five criteria: dental history, medical history, teeth present, diagnosis, treatment plan
audits.setting: Prosthodontics department, King's College London Dental Institute, Guy's Hospital

cycle1.result: 8% of letters met all five criteria; 11% met none.

audits.intervention: Letters sent to referring practitioners requesting better information.

cycle2.result: 9% met all five criteria; 15% met none.

audits.citation: Fenlon MR, Glick S, Sherriff M. An audit of letters of referral to a prosthodontic department in a dental teaching hospital. Eur J Prosthodont Restor Dent. 2008;16(3):128-131. PMID: 19051555.

audits.title: An audit of patient referrals to the sedation department of Newcastle Dental Hospital.
audits.standard: SIGN recommendations for referral information for sedation
audits.setting: Department of Sedation, Newcastle Dental Hospital

cycle1.result: Medical history provided in 59.0% of referrals and previous dental treatment in 27.5%; 76% were letters and 24% pro forma.

audits.other_findings: Pro forma improved some items (telephone number, medication, doctor details) but had less referrer information; guidelines or electronic templates suggested.
audits.citation: Dentith GE, Wilson KE, Dorman M, Girdler NM. An audit of patient referrals to the sedation department of Newcastle Dental Hospital. Prim Dent Care. 2010;17(2):85-91. doi:10.1308/135576110791013857. PMID: 20353657.

audits.title: An audit of the quality of referral letters received by the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, Dublin Dental School and Hospital.
audits.setting: Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, Dublin Dental School and Hospital

cycle1.result: Referral letters in general required modification and did not give the required information.

audits.other_findings: A referral template is proposed for future referrals.

audits.title: The effects of audit and feedback and electronic referrals on the quality of primary care referral letters.
audits.setting: 15 GPs and 2 nurses, West Coast general practices (Greymouth)
audits.intervention: Written feedback on referral letter quality; later introduction of electronic referrals

cycle2.result: Average score improved to 86.9% after feedback.

audits.other_findings: Electronic referral letters, assessed a further five months later, gave no further improvement.
audits.citation: Corwin P, Bolter T. The effects of audit and feedback and electronic referrals on the quality of primary care referral letters. J Prim Health Care. 2014;6(4):324-327. doi:10.1071/hc14324. PMID: 25485329.

audits.title: Orthodontic referrals: why do GDPs get it wrong?
audits.setting: Orthodontic diagnostic teaching clinics, King's College Hospital, London
audits.intervention: Referral guidelines and pathway sent back to referring practitioners.
audits.other_findings: Poor IOTN use, low IOTN scores, poor oral hygiene, caries, early or adult referrals; authors suggest proformas.
audits.citation: Reddy S, Derringer KA, Rennie L. Orthodontic referrals: why do GDPs get it wrong?. Br Dent J. 2016;221(9):583-587. doi:10.1038/sj.bdj.2016.826. PMID: 27811869.

audits.title: Initial periodontal therapy before referring a patient: an audit.
audits.standard: British Society of Periodontology referral criteria: all patients should have initial periodontal therapy before referral
audits.setting: Eastman Dental Hospital restorative dentistry referrals

cycle1.result: All 100 referrals incomplete; 12 had BPE scores matching those at consultation; 85 patients reported oral hygiene instruction and 91 root surface debridement before referral.

audits.other_findings: Most referrers gave no diagnosis and used incorrect terminology; 25 dentists reported more initial therapy than patients did.
audits.citation: Kalsi AS, Darbar U. Initial periodontal therapy before referring a patient: an audit. Br Dent J. 2019;227(11):977-983. doi:10.1038/s41415-019-1048-2. PMID: 31844227.
